learning_outcomes.text: Explains the basic types, structures, components, and operating principles of load transmission machines (continuous and discrete).
Understands the mechanical properties and operating principles of lifting machines, cranes, hoists, hoists, elevators, and similar systems.
Calculates the capacity, strength, and performance of continuous and discrete load transmission machines.
Analyzes brake and elevator systems using engineering principles and performs calculations for sample applications.
Evaluates transport and lifting machines within the framework of standards and regulations and applies safety criteria.

syllabus_topics: General information, to introduce the lesson plan. Load types, continuous and discontinuous transport machines.
Structures, the parts and working mechanics of elevation machines.
The parts of cranes (rope, chain, hook, companion flange, pulley and pulley systems) and strength computations
Structures, the parts and working mechanics of travelling crane, simple pulley block, Weston pulley block, workshop hoist, worm screw pulley block and computations of application.
Continuous transport machines, working mechanics, load capacities computations.
Structures, the parts and working mechanics of belt conveyor and computations of application.
Structures, the parts and working mechanics of belt conveyor and computations of application.
Structures, the parts and working mechanics of worm conveyor and computations of application.
Discontinuous transport machines, vehicles; structures, the parts and working mechanics of work trucks and work machines.
The computations and applications of discontinuous transport machines.
Working structures and mechanic of brake systems at transport machines and vehicles.
Structures, the parts and working mechanics of elevators.
Standards and regulations on transport systems.
